newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan, Libya provoke civil strife - Somali warlord.
newsitem.headline: Sudan, Libya provoke civil strife - Somali warlord.

text.p: One of the main Somali warlords said in an interview published on Thursday that Sudan and Libya were helping to prolong the civil war in his country.
"Our problem is attributable...to (interference by) countries like Sudan and Libya," Ali Mahdi Mohamed, leader of a clan alliance, told the London-based Arabic daily al-Hayat.
He said his alliance had asked the two governments to withdraw their representatives from Somalia. "But they opted to provoke the Somali people in this critical stage," he added.
A series of conferences in Mogadishu and regional capitals have failed to bring peace to Somalia, which has had no central government since late president Mohamed Siad Barre fell in 1991.
Ali Mahdi said that Sudanese military officers were working in south Mogadishu for his rival leader Hussein Aideed, leader of the Somali National Alliance (SNA).
Hussein, 34, was elected by supporters as president of Somalia, replacing his father Mohamed Farah Aideed, who died of wounds sustained during a fight in the capital.
Ali Mahdi also says he is president and rejects the Aideed government, recognised only by Sudan and Libya.
"We know, from reliable sources, that six Sudanese military officers are working in south Mogadishu for Aideed's clan," Ali Mahdi told the daily from his north Mogadishu stronghold.
"Sudan has played a role in the past enmities among Somali tribes. This (Sudanese) government has become like a cancer which threatens our existence," he added.
"The Libyan representative in south Mogadishu, Mustafa Salem al-Amoush, encouraged Aideed to wage an attack against the southwest town of Baidoa," he said.
Aideed seized Baidoa in September last year in a fight that killed hundreds of people.
